3. That the suit was filed on the allegation that the property appertaining to Petty Settlement Khatian No. 176 of Mouza Patharghata, Police Station Patharghata measuring 13.73 acres of land belonged to Afezuddin in eight annas share and Mominuddin owned seven annas share and Mati Bibi owned one anna share. Afezuddin sold 2.40 acres of land to different persons and Mominuddin sold 1.60 acres to different persons and Mati Bibi got her .78 acres of land recorded in the name of her sons through Nikah marriage. 

 4. It was further alleged that the land of the Petty Settlement Khatian increased by .15 acres to 13.88 acres and one Ismail was entrusted with the task of preparing the Khatian and got the same recorded wrongly. The plaintiff opposite party was enjoying 9.01 acres of land and the defendant-petitioners refused to partition the suit land on 15.5.2000 and hence the present suit was filed. 

 5. That the Defendant-Respondent-petitioner filed a written statement alleging inter alia that the suit is not maintainable, barred by limitation and it was further alleged that the suit property belonged to Afezuddin, Mominuddin and Mati Bibi and Mati Biubi transferred to son Mominddin and 2nd husband Ainuddin and thereafter they transferred their interest in favour of predecessor of defendant number 35, Mominuddin and their names was recorded in Revisional Settlement Khatian no. 202 and Mominuddin on 15.03.1937 sold the same to Serajuddin thereafter Mominuddin also sold .88 acres of land to Hazrat Ali and others. Mominuddin transferred .88 acres of land to Joinuddin and it was recorded in the names of four sons of Jainuddin and the recorded tenant on 13.3.1952 transferred the same in favour of defendant no. 31 Kashem Ali and it was recorded in Khatian no. 104, Momin uddin transferred 3.90 acres of land in favour of Moslem Ali and others and their names were recorded in the Revisional Settlement Khatian. Afezuddin transferred 3.96 acres of land in favour of Prayan Bala and their name was recorded in Revisional Settlement Khatian. Prayan Bala and Kiron Bala sold .91 acres of land in favour of Ismail Dafadar, Hazrat Ali and others who sold to Malek and others and it was recorded in their name as such during the Revisional Settlement operation. Afezuddin sold 2.60 acres of land in favour of Sherjan Ali and others which was recorded in their name and thus the Petty Settlement recorded tenants transferred their entire right and to Keron Bala who sold her rest of the land to Ismail and Kashem and it was also alleged that 2.83 acres of land was acquired by Government where construction was made by Government. The Revisional Settlement and State Acquisition Khatian are correct and defendant no. 31 filed a separate written statement and he claimed 1.28 acres of land by successive purchase. 

 9. The learned Counsel Mr. Ali Reza with Mr. Salim Reza, appearing on behalf of the Defendant-Respondent-petitioner submits that the learned Appellate court was absolutely wrong and erroneous in reversing the Judgment and decree passed by the trial court. The trial court after consideration of the evidence on record documents and exhibits and other connected papers came to a proper and justified finding in dismissing the suit of the plaintiffs because the plaintiffs could not successfully proved the case. The learned counsel further submits that the trial court found in his Judgment that the documents filed by the defendants were executed by Momin uddin and Afezuddin and thereby their right title and interest in the suit land was extinguished. He next submits that the learned trial court observed in his Judgment that Momin uddin transferred his entire share to the predecessors of the defendants but the learned, appellate court although discussed about the share of Afezuddin but he remained silent with regard to the share of Momin uddin. The learned appellate court without considering the materials evidence on record and without applying his judicial mind and without proper assessment of evidence on record came to a wrong and erroneous finding in reversing the Judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court. The learned counsel also submits that onus of proving a case upon the plaintiffs but not upon the weakness and short coming of the defendants. The appellate court only discussed about the weakness and shorting coming of the defendant but how far the plaintiffs could be able to prove their case that was not taken into consideration by the learned appellate court. The appellate court ought to have been considered that the R.S and S.A. Khatian were prepared in the name of the defendants and the defendants regularly paying the rents. Defendant-Respondent-petitioners produced and exhibited the certified copy of the R.S. and S.A. Khatian which has been marked as exhibit-A and B series. The defendants also produced the rent receipts which were marked as Exhibit-D series and certified copy of the documents were exhibited and marked as C- series. The learned counsel finally submits that the appellate court by misreading the evidence on record and by non consideration of the material documentary evidence came to a wrong and fallacious finding in reversing the Judgment and decree of the trial court occasioning failure of justice which is liable to be interfere by this Court and hence, the rule should be made absolute.
